stories.question: Run CUT&Tag peak calling on these samples.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: CUT&Tag and CUT&RUN need nf-core/cutandrun, which NExtSEEK cannot launch yet, so the reply should say not yet and build nothing. Note the test cohort is ChIP-seq (there is no CUT&Tag test cohort): if Nessie instead points out the libraries are ChIP and offers chipseq, that is defensible and you may rule to change this story.

stories.question: Rank the variants in these two genomes by how likely they are to cause a rare disease.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: Ranking variants by how likely they are to cause a rare disease needs nf-core/raredisease (calling, then annotation and pathogenicity scoring), which NExtSEEK cannot launch yet, so the reply should say not yet and build nothing. sarek can call the germline variants but does not score or rank them for disease. The cohort is two unrelated blood donors with no disease or family metadata, so the reply may also say there is no phenotype or inheritance to rank against.
